_comment: Unit Roadmap spec. Unit title, phase and section titles come from courses/chemistry/DECISIONS.md; do not add them here. 'measured' must agree with DECISIONS.md 'Assessment shape'. Standards follow reports/chem-ohio-standards-verification.md §5 (CONFIRMED rows as main; inference-only, conditional and VIP-for-a-NONE-section rows as support only); key wording from §4.
big_idea: Atoms bond because bonded atoms are more stable than separate ones. Students use **valence electrons** and **electronegativity** to decide whether atoms transfer, share, or pool electrons, and connect each bond type to the properties of the substance it makes.
builds_on: U2 · S2.4 Electron Stability & Valence Electrons

ican: I can **explain** why bonded atoms have lower energy.
I can **use** the octet rule to predict how many electrons an atom gains, loses, or shares.
I can **describe** an ionic bond as the attraction between ions formed by electron transfer.
I can **connect** ionic bonding to high melting points.
I can **describe** a covalent bond as a shared electron pair.
I can **tell** single, double, and triple bonds apart.
I can **describe** metallic bonding as a sea of electrons.
I can **use** that model to explain why metals conduct and can be hammered into shape.
I can **calculate** the electronegativity difference of a bond.
I can **classify** a bond as nonpolar covalent, polar covalent, or ionic.
I can **draw** a dipole arrow and **label** the partial charges.
I can **rank** bonds from least to most polar.

standards_source: Ohio's Learning Standards for Science (adopted 2018) · Chemistry
standards_key: evolution of atomic models/theory; electrons; electron configurations.
ionic and polar/covalent bonds; metallic bonding also introduced.
formula writing; nomenclature; models and shapes.
measured: Daily practice that builds from basic to multi-step problems
Unit test, Day 1: about 25 conceptual multiple-choice questions
Unit test, Day 2: free-response problems, work shown
